newsitem.title: USA: Judge relinquishes top spot on Illinois court.
newsitem.headline: Judge relinquishes top spot on Illinois court.

text.p: James Heiple stepped aside as chief justice of the Illinois Supreme Court Friday, two days after a disciplinary commission censured him for disreputable behaviour.
Heiple will remain on the court but still faces an impeachment proceeding in the state legislature. He had been chosen chief judge for a three-year term by his six fellow justices in January.
On Wednesday, the five-member Illinois Courts Commission unanimously agreed to censure Heiple for what it said was disreputable behaviour when he was stopped for traffic violations.

The members of the commission, which included a chairman hand-picked by Heiple, ruled that he violated Supreme Court rules and it "further determined that (his) conduct was prejudicial to the administration of justice and brought the judicial office into disrepute."

The commission held a hearing earlier last month for Heiple at which he did not dispute the facts of the case, precluding the appearance of any witnesses. After the hearing, he defended his actions to reporters and complained that the police had treated him roughly, demonstrating how he was flung across the hood of his car.

Heiple was arrested after he allegedly ignored an order to stop his car. Other police officers later alleged that they had stopped him in the past for traffic offences but that he had flashed his court credentials and been allowed to go free.

He has also been criticised for some controversial opinions, most notably one involving "Baby Richard," a Chicago-area child who was returned to his natural parents years after his birth mother had given him up for adoption.
Illinois Lt. Gov. Bob Kustra said Friday that Heiple had made a "good move" by relinquishing the chief justice's chair but said he still thought he should have quit the court completely.
